title: Implement a structured Vaporize IssueReporter without replacing the default reporter
createdBy: codex@loom from the Vaporize runtime visibility gap

historicalContent.description: Define VaporizeIssueEvent and a Sendable IssueReporter that appends one event per report to a request-scoped sink. Register it alongside IssueReporter.default so Xcode runtime warnings and native test failures continue to work.
acceptanceCriteria: VaporizeIssueEvent is Codable, Sendable, versioned, and stable under round-trip tests.
The reporter performs concurrency-safe JSONL append with one complete record per issue.
Registration appends the Vaporize reporter to the existing reporters rather than replacing IssueReporter.default.
Reporter sink failure uses a non-recursive stderr fallback and cannot crash the consumer process.
Message and source-path redaction rules are explicit and tested before events enter durable receipts.
Expected and unexpected issue events remain distinguishable.
No production fatality policy is embedded in the reporter; escalation remains caller or environment policy.

implementationEvidence.testProof: Vaporize toolchain swift test --filter VaporizeIssueReporterTests passed 7 tests in 1 suite, including 32 concurrent reports and the non-recursive sink-failure fallback.
implementationEvidence.registrationProof: The install and scoped APIs append VaporizeIssueReporter to IssueReporters.current rather than replacing Point-Free's default reporter.
implementationEvidence.expectedIssueBoundary: Swift Testing native known-issue state is paired with VaporizeIssueReporting.withExpectedReporter because upstream expectation state is not propagated to appended custom reporters.
implementationEvidence.ingestionBoundary: This reporter emits request-scoped JSONL. Vaporize test receipt ingestion is implemented; run launch ingestion and the IRC consumer pilot remain separate open beads.
